items.readable_text:
Content:
The advantage of box models over area models is that box models can be used to solve division problems with remainders.

Content:
To demonstrate, let's find the quotient and remainder of the following division problem:

Content:
[MATH: 83 \div 6]

Content:
First, we write our division in the usual way.

Content:
| | | |
| | [MATH: 6] | | | | [MATH: 8] | [MATH: 3] | | | |

Content:
Filling in our box model by applying our usual method, we get the following:

Content:
| | [MATH: 10] | [MATH: \color{blue}3] |
| | [MATH: 6] | | | | [MATH: 8] | [MATH: 3] | | / | [MATH: -] | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: 0] | | / | | [MATH: \color{red}2] | [MATH: \color{red}3] | | | | | [MATH: \color{red}2] | [MATH: \color{red}3] | | / | [MATH: -] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 8] | | / | | | [MATH: \fbox{5}] | | |

Content:
Now, note the following:

Content:
- The result of the final subtraction is [MATH: \fbox{5},] not zero.
- However, we cannot subtract any further since [MATH: \fbox{5}] is less than our divisor [MATH: 6.]
- Therefore, [MATH: \fbox{5}] is the remainder!

Content:
The quotient is the sum of the numbers on top of the boxes:
[MATH: 10+3=13]

Content:
Therefore, the solution to our division problem is
[MATH: 83 \div 6 = 13 \,\text{R}\, \fbox{5}.]

Content:
Let's see another example.

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The advantage of box models over area models is that box models can be used to solve division problems with remainders.

Content:
To demonstrate, let's find the quotient and remainder of the following division problem:

Content:
[MATH: 83 \div 6]

Content:
First, we write our division in the usual way.

Content:
| | | |
| | [MATH: 6] | | | | [MATH: 8] | [MATH: 3] | | | |

Content:
Filling in our box model by applying our usual method, we get the following:

Content:
| | [MATH: 10] | [MATH: \color{blue}3] |
| | [MATH: 6] | | | | [MATH: 8] | [MATH: 3] | | / | [MATH: -] | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: 0] | | / | | [MATH: \color{red}2] | [MATH: \color{red}3] | | | | | [MATH: \color{red}2] | [MATH: \color{red}3] | | / | [MATH: -] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 8] | | / | | | [MATH: \fbox{5}] | | |

Content:
Now, note the following:

Content:
- The result of the final subtraction is [MATH: \fbox{5},] not zero.
- However, we cannot subtract any further since [MATH: \fbox{5}] is less than our divisor [MATH: 6.]
- Therefore, [MATH: \fbox{5}] is the remainder!

Content:
The quotient is the sum of the numbers on top of the boxes:
[MATH: 10+3=13]

Content:
Therefore, the solution to our division problem is
[MATH: 83 \div 6 = 13 \,\text{R}\, \fbox{5}.]

Content:
Let's see another example.
